What normalization did — and did not do

The lightweight Sharp + pure-JavaScript prototype uses threshold-connected contours, convex-hull quadrilateral proposals, all-four-edge Sobel support, conservative area/aspect/perspective checks, projective resampling, portrait-axis alignment and contain padding to 600×900. No dependencies were added. It does not simply resize the whole photo to 2:3.

Scan 3113 is the sole accepted geometric detection. Visual inspection of its outline shows the card face isolated from much of the surrounding tabletop/cards. All other scans failed safely with byte-identical originals; therefore surrounding hand/table/background removal is not reliable on this cohort. Sleeves/toploaders remain problematic: there is no semantic inner-card detector; competing rectangle proposals trigger fallback, but a single sleeve outline can still fool this geometry-only method. No claim of general card-only detection success is made.

Upright 180° orientation cannot be established by this method without semantic evidence; no guessed 180° rotation is performed. Severe perspective is rejected. Rectified proportions use mean opposite edge lengths followed by uniform contain padding; exact physical aspect under perspective is not recoverable from this uncalibrated single view, so absence of all projective distortion is not proven. Clipping is not automatically verifiable.

Five failure examples: 3032, 3035, 3038, 3040 and 3046 found no complete high-support card boundary and retained the raw image. Helped/hurt rank examples: none evaluable because all correct references are absent. Scan 3113 changed its wrong top candidate from #11868 to #11379; higher distractor similarity is not evidence of improvement.

Synthetic rotated and mild-perspective cases passed detection and 600×900 output checks. Four projective corner mappings passed numerical checks. A uniform image failed detection and preserved exact raw bytes. These simple synthetic successes do not establish real-photo reliability.

Conflicts are derived from explicit scan-linked historical collector feedback versus the current manual ID, not frozen matcher predictions: 3055: 17857 vs 17910; 3091: 20613 vs 20604; 3129: 198 vs 17202. Structured side === back classifications are checked. Conservative equivalence permits only exact same IDs unless independently verified evidence exists. Updated eligibility validation reproduced the same frozen 16 cases; raw results needed no rerun.

The canonical single-image model dinov2-small:c2bb04a51fab207c420665f1946016107bffc701:q8:cls:rgb-fit224-v1 generated fresh CLS query embeddings separately for both runs. No pooling, dimensionality, model, index vectors or production pipeline changes. Existing ready references are restricted to current eligible catalog fronts exactly as the service does and loaded in a read-only repeatable-read DEV transaction. After freezing, the second run accesses only this local snapshot.

Search uses canonical normalized vectors cast to Float32, canonical visualTopK for the ten reference URLs, plus canonical exact cosine over every frozen reference for full-rank auditing. Reference full-sort ties use URL lexical order; ranked URLs expand to all current IDs sharing that URL, then card ties are ordered by ascending numeric card ID. The displayed top 10 and correct ranks are deterministic card-level ranks. Reference top-K tie behavior remains the canonical heap behavior over key-ordered snapshot input. No text, OCR, set/year/number, historical candidates or labels enter vector ranking; names/IDs resolve only after similarity calculation.

Verified: all 31 saved decision-associated originals retain their provenance SHA-256; manual decisions unchanged; frozen reference hash unchanged; 15 raw fallbacks produced identical fresh embeddings and rankings across runs. Reference SHA-256: 711c98c7d9a623765f5515d75f1043a6e559c4db9dca0d4f6f5c5781d757e9da. Decisions SHA-256: 7c4b73235ef2978bb90aaebc216b6c95d41c36a9866888469058812c362f2285. Original hashes, conflict evidence and QA results are embedded in the downloadable JSON. The preserved 958-vector snapshot and fresh query vectors remain in local experiment files; they are not redundantly embedded in this compact report.

Recommendation — bounded next test, separately authorized

Do not change the model or interpret this as evidence against image-first DINO. First, in a later separately authorized experiment, verify independent, correct front references for these 16 labels (especially the reviewer-reported wrong stored image for 3130), then index only those verified references while preserving these same 958 distractors. Exclude original-scan/self-copy leakage. Repeat the frozen-cohort comparison with real coverage. That indexing was not performed here. Improve and validate normalization conservatively before considering deployment; current real-photo detection is insufficient.

No full/bulk indexing was started. Indexing remains paused by this experiment. No labels, originals, Cloudinary assets, catalog, user collections, ownership, app routes or review UI were changed. Nothing was published; production was not accessed or changed.

Standalone private development report. It contains saved scan previews and can be viewed offline without contacting external services.
